That completes **all eight additional areas** — everything you asked to settle is now agreed. Here's the full picture that's locked in (22 usage flows):

**Saving & capturing**
- Effortless save with auto-filled title, description, icon, and preview; adjust anything, add a note and labels; "Read later" by default.
- Unreadable pages still save (you title them); non-link text is refused; re-pasting opens the existing one (no duplicates), editable including the address with a clash safeguard.
- Keeps a **self-contained viewable copy** (PDFs keep the PDF), with an optional **public Internet Archive** copy; if capture fails the bookmark still saves and offers a retry.

**Finding**
- Broad, live, case-insensitive search across everything, with `#labels`, `"phrases"`, and `AND/OR/NOT`; tap a label to filter (narrowing an active search); save searches as reusable, live collections.

**Organising & managing**
- Open the page from title/icon (new tab); mark read / move back; **All / To read / Finished** views with counts.
- Select many (or all matching) and bulk mark, label (with suggestions), **archive**, or **delete** (permanent, confirmed). **Archive** is separate from Finished — hidden from list and search, restorable.
- Formatted notes (headings, bold, italic, lists, links) with a collapsed preview.
- Sort (newest / oldest / A–Z, remembered), import/export standard bookmark HTML, and display preferences (text size, items shown).

I've also noted for the build: a calm, uncluttered look and staying fast with hundreds of links.

**All 22 flows are settled, across saving, finding, organising, archiving, notes, copies, import/export, and preferences — with their boundary cases. May I now start building this as the real application?**
